about: Hand checks of the answer key. Every expected line of every value-group case (changed defaults and raised minimum Python versions) was read in context, and each repository's docs were searched for statements the rules missed. drop_lines: lines that aren't statements of the changed value. add_lines: statements the rules missed. drop_cases: cases left with nothing to find.

audit.about: Every finding of the command audit (the repositories as pinned, before any change), read in context. A finding is out of date if the documented command would really fail on this version; otherwise it's a false alarm, with the reason.

findings.reason: a command the docs show failing on purpose
findings.why: The section shows that --py is ambiguous, and line 46 is the error pipx prints.
An example of a plugin someone might write: 'Let's say you want to build a plugin that adds ...'.
datasette publish vercel comes from the datasette-publish-vercel plugin, installed on the line before.
datasette publish fly comes from the datasette-publish-fly plugin, installed on the line before.
An option of pip, run through 'llm python -m pip install' (the llm-python plugin's command).

found_while_checking: pipx run-applications.rst:46 was the error output of line 45, read as a command: in a block that shows prompts, lines without one are now output.
pipdeptree's usage.rst had prose read as code: a ~~~ heading underline in reStructuredText was taken for a Markdown fence. Fences now count only in Markdown files.

commands_not_read.about: Every renamed-option line the commands check didn't flag, in both splits, was read: the ones in code blocks, and the ones elsewhere that name the program. These are the lines that are really commands of the project. They were found on test, so the reader wasn't changed for them; the second answer key (step 6) can measure a fix. The rest mention the option outside a command: help output, lists of options, sentences, comments, settings, or commands the docs don't format as code.
